title: Our values, in practice
vimeoName: Belong School · Module 3 · Values in Practice

segments.text: Every company has values. Most of them live on a wall in a meeting room and die
there. I want ours to live in your hands, in the decisions you make when nobody's
watching, when the day is long, when the guest is difficult, when the easy choice
and the right choice are not the same choice.
So let's go through them, not as a list to memorize, as tools to use.
Sustainability, and I always insist on saying it fully: financial, environmental,
and social sustainability. All three in that unusual order on purpose.
People are sometimes surprised I put financial first.
Let me be honest with you about why.
If Craveiral doesn't make money, everything else dies.
The farm dies, the jobs die, the mission dies.
The whole beautiful idea becomes a story about a lawyer who wasted his money on a
dream. Financial sustainability is what buys us the right to pursue everything
else. So when you avoid waste, when you take care of equipment, when you fill the
washing machine properly, when you upsell a wine you believe in, you're not being
petty, you're protecting the mission.
Environmental sustainability, you already know.
The 4% footprint, the water recycling, the composting, the regenerative farming.
And social aspect, fair work, local hiring, serving the village, being a good
neighbor. Three legs. The stool stands on all of them or it doesn't stand.
Simplicity. This one is deceptive because simplicity is hard work.
Anyone can make something complicated.
Look at our houses, minimalist design, natural materials, nothing shouting for
attention. That's a thousand decisions about what to leave out.
In your work, simplicity means don't overcomplicate the guest experience.
Clear answers, honest food, processes that make sense.
If you find yourself doing something convoluted and you don't know why, question
it. Ask. Maybe there's a reason. Maybe it's just accumulated clutter and you found
something we should simplify. Comfort and modernity.
We are rustic in soul, but we are not a museum of rural hardship.
Our guests sleep on excellent mattresses. The indoor pool is heated.
The Wi-Fi works. There are Smeg appliances and We-Wood furniture in some of the
houses. And every house has a proper kitchen and a private terrace.
Why does this matter? Because we're not asking guests to sacrifice comfort in
exchange for authenticity. The whole point of Craveiral is that they get both.
Simplicity is not scarcity. Remember that when you set up a room or serve a table,
warm, generous, comfortable, and simple.
Freedom and authenticity. Guests at Craveiral are free.
Free to do everything, surf lessons, horseback riding, hikes on the fisherman's
trail, yoga, or absolutely gloriously nothing.
Never make a guest feel they're missing out if they just want to lie by the pool
for three days. And authenticity means we don't perform.
The farm is a real farm. The eggs are real eggs from this morning.
The people are real people. You are not required to wear a corporate smile that
isn't yours. I would much rather a guest meet the real you with your real warmth
and your real accent than some hospitality school character.
Guests can smell theater from a kilometer away. What they can't resist is truth.
Creativity and community integration. Creativity.
You're allowed to have ideas. More than allowed, expected.
Some of the best things at Craveiral came from the team, not from me.
And community integration. We are of São Teotónio, not just in it.
The laundry serves the village. The shop sells our neighbors honey and wine and
olive oil. We hire locally whenever we can.
When a guest asks what to visit, we send them to the village, to Odeceixe, to
Zambujeira, to the local restaurants.
We are ambassadors for the whole territory, not gatekeepers trying to trap guests
on the property. Well-being, and this one is for the guests and for you.
A burned-out team cannot deliver warm hospitality.
It's simply not possible to give what you don't have.
So take your breaks, eat properly. Tell your manager when the load is too much.
Use the beauty of this place. You work somewhere people pay hundreds of euros a
night to be. Walk the property sometimes. Look at the coastline on your day off.
If working here doesn't include some joy, we're doing it wrong, and I want to know.
Now, values are easy when everything's fine. The test is when they conflict.
A guest wants something wasteful. Comfort versus sustainability.
A creative idea costs money. Creativity versus financial discipline.
I'm not going to pretend there's a formula. There isn't.
What I'll tell you is this: when values collide, think about the long game.
We're not trying to win a day. We're trying to build something that lasts decades.
The decision that serves the relationship with the guest, with the land, with the
team. Over the years, that's almost always the right one.
And when you're not sure, ask. Asking is never a weakness here.
Next model, we get the craft itself. Hospitality, the Craveiral way.
